title: When the Extraction Breaks
premise: Rosalind Nystrom, a deniable fixer for a diplomatic mission that exists only in sealed annexes, is summoned when a dead colleague's voiceprint unlocks a server in Singapore containing proof that the embassy's founding charter was funded by laundered inheritance money. As rival intelligence services and the family whose fortune built the institution close in, Rosalind discovers his own identity was manufactured as part of the cover-up. He must decide whether to sell the secret to a Frankfurt hedge fund manager who can expose it before markets open, or destroy it and preserve the fragile peace it underwrites. In the end he leaks only half the truth — enough to burn the guilty family, keep the embassy alive, and walk away with a name that finally belongs to him.
about_author: Marguerite Lockridge is the pen name of a former compliance analyst who spent a decade inside cross-border financial institutions before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about paper trails, quiet violence, and the people paid to make both disappear.

chapters.title: The Voiceprint
chapters.summary: POV: Rosalind. A routine document handoff in Vienna is interrupted when Rosalind learns that Marcus Hale, a fixer presumed dead for three years, has just authenticated into an embassy server from Singapore using his own archived voiceprint. The emotional beat is cold unease — the machinery Rosalind trusts has begun speaking with a dead man's voice, and he is ordered to treat it as a security exercise rather than a resurrection.

chapters.title: Annex Nine
chapters.summary: POV: Rosalind, with a flashback interlude from Hale's journal. Rosalind digs into Annex Nine, the sealed charter establishing the embassy, and finds funding routed through a trust belonging to the Voss family, whose patriarch died owing debts to people who don't exist. The beat is dawning dread: the institution isn't compromised; it was built dirty from day one.

chapters.title: Singapore Hours
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Rosalind and Ilse Brandt, a Frankfurt fund analyst. Rosalind flies to Singapore and finds Hale alive, paranoid, living off cash and burner phones. Hale claims the server holds evidence that would collapse the embassy and half the European bond market tied to Voss holdings. Beat: wary alliance between two men trained never to trust anyone.

chapters.title: What the Charter Bought
chapters.summary: POV: Rosalind. Inside a data center in Jurong, Hale shows him the archive: fifteen years of payments proving the embassy's operations were collateralized against stolen Voss inheritance. Rosalind realizes his own employment file predates his earliest memory of himself. Beat: vertigo — the investigation turns inward, and identity itself becomes the crime scene.

chapters.title: The Family Business
chapters.summary: POV: Anneliese Voss. The Voss heiress, learning the server exists, activates private contractors she's kept on retainer since her father's death. She believes the archive is hers by blood right and will kill to reclaim it. Beat: chilling competence — the antagonist is introduced not as a villain but as someone protecting an inheritance with total conviction.

chapters.title: Rules That Get Rewritten
chapters.summary: POV: Rosalind. Summoned home, Rosalind is offered promotion and erasure in one breath: retire quietly, or be retired. His handler reveals Rosalind's identity was fabricated to give the embassy a clean-faced operative untraceable to the Voss money. Beat: betrayal crystallizing into resolve — he stops following rules that were written to bury him.

chapters.title: Half a Truth
chapters.summary: POV: Ilse Brandt. Ilse receives an anonymous approach offering the Voss dossier ahead of Frankfurt's opening bell, and begins verifying it while her firm's lawyers circle. Meanwhile contractors hit Hale's safehouse; he escapes wounded. Beat: accelerating clock — the market deadline becomes literal, and every party now knows everyone else is moving.

chapters.title: Frankfurt Before the Bell
chapters.summary: POV: Rosalind. Rosalind smuggles Hale out through Rotterdam and races to Frankfurt, trading the archive's location to Ilse in exchange for broadcast access at market open. Contractors and Anneliese converge on the exchange. Beat: high-velocity climax setup — the trade is made, the price is his own history, and there is no version where he walks out unchanged.

chapters.title: Opening Bell
chapters.summary: POV: Rosalind and Anneliese. On the exchange floor, Rosalind releases half the dossier — enough to freeze Voss assets and trigger investigations, but not enough to topple the embassy. Anneliese confronts him; Hale takes a bullet meant for Rosalind and survives barely. Beat: climax — justice delivered surgically, outside any courtroom, at the cost of everything Rosalind pretended to be.

chapters.title: A Name That Fits
chapters.summary: POV: Rosalind, epilogue six months later. The embassy endures, cleaned and quieter; Anneliese faces prosecutors armed with the leaked half; Hale recovers under a new name of his own choosing. Rosalind, officially erased, keeps the only copy of the full truth — leverage or legacy, undecided. Beat: bittersweet resolution — he ends with no country, no employer, and for the first time, a self he authored.
